TEAM DESCRIPTION 

Our team is working on software to monitor and support astronaut health during space missions. We’re looking for teammates skilled or interested in software development, AI/ML, data analysis, UI/UX, biomedical science, or space science. Join us to combine our skills and build an innovative, practical solution for the challenge
summary:
SpaceMed: An Integrated Astronaut Health Monitoring System

SpaceMed is a web-based astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support crew health and well-being during long-duration space missions. It integrates multiple health-monitoring domains, including physiological indicators, metabolic and hydration status, sleep and circadian health, musculoskeletal health, stress, mood, and cognitive performance. The platform incorporates daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly monitoring, alongside AI-assisted health intelligence, cognitive testing, crew health monitoring, and a digital twin concept to help interpret health trends and identify potential risks.

SpaceMed addresses the challenges of spaceflight, where microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation, sleep disruption, and demanding mission conditions can affect astronauts' physical and cognitive performance. By bringing diverse health indicators into one integrated platform, it aims to support continuous monitoring, early risk awareness, and more informed health-management decisions. This is important because maintaining astronaut health is essential for crew safety, mission performance, and the success of future long-duration space exploration.
details: Project Details – SpaceMed SpaceMed is an integrated astronaut health-monitoring platform designed to address the physical, physiological and cognitive challenges associated with long-duration space missions. It provides a unified digital environment for monitoring multiple dimensions of astronaut health, helping identify potential health risks and understand changes in crew well-being over time. The platform works through interconnected monitoring modules covering physiological health, metabolic and hydration status, sleep and circadian health, musculoskeletal health, stress and mood, and cognitive performance. It incorporates daily, weekly, monthly and yearly monitoring to distinguish immediate health variations from longer-term trends. Its cognitive reaction-time testing module evaluates aspects of cognitive performance, while AI-assisted Health Intelligence analyses available health indicators to highlight potential risks and contributing factors. Additional features include Crew Health monitoring and a Digital Twin concept for exploring interconnected health systems. The primary benefit of SpaceMed is the integration of diverse health indicators into one platform rather than treating each health parameter independently. This can help mission teams interpret health trends, recognise potential warning signs and make more informed health-management decisions. Its intended impact is to contribute to safer space missions, improved astronaut well-being and better preparation for long-duration exploration. The project was developed using HTML for the frontend and Python for the backend, with web-based technologies for its interactive interface and data processing. The development focused on accessibility, modularity, scientific relevance and the possibility of future integration with persistent databases and real astronaut health-monitoring systems. SpaceMed's creativity lies in its holistic approach: connecting physiological, metabolic, musculoskeletal, psychological and neurocognitive monitoring within a single framework. The team considered the distinctive conditions of spaceflight, including microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation, circadian disruption, limited resources and the need for continuous health assessment. The project aims to evolve into an integrated decision-support system for future human space exploration.
